sampling_model.design: One-shot finite-population randomization across \(C\) fixed clusters. Independently across clusters, the known mechanism draws either an exact-count label with probabilities converging to \(r\), or a nominal Bernoulli saturation label with probabilities converging to \(p\).
sampling_model.units: Each cluster contains \(n_0\) units and carries an unrestricted fixed binary potential-outcome vector for every within-cluster assignment; there is no cross-cluster interference.
sampling_model.treatment: Exact-count assignment samples uniformly from \(\mathcal S_k\); nominal label \(\ell\) treats units independently with probability \(m_\ell/n_0\), so target-hit rates equal \(Bp\).
sampling_model.overlap: Exact-count designs lie in \(\Delta_K(\rho)\); every entry of \(B\) is positive for interior target counts.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The table \(f\), hence \(\mu_z\), is fixed external planning information or comes from an external pilot. The calibrated Horvitz--Thompson estimator uses these fixed centers and known hit probabilities; the current trial does not estimate \(\Xi\), and optimization protects against every coupling in \(\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\).
sampling_model.randomness: Potential outcomes are fixed; all probability, expectation, convergence, and regret statements are with respect to the known assignment mechanism only.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Derives sharp bounds on the scalar variance of the difference-in-means estimator from two marginal potential-outcome distributions.
Casts causal partial identification with multiple potential outcomes as a multi-marginal optimal-transport problem and derives exact identified sets.
Characterizes admissible conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and optimizes the selected bound by a convex program for fixed experimental designs and linear estimators.
Provides randomization-based inference and power analysis for direct and spillover effects under a fixed two-stage design distribution.
Uses variance and power formulas to study saturation design under maintained treatment and spillover structures.
Establishes finite-population central limit theorems for multiple treatment levels, factors, and vector outcomes under assignment-only randomness.
Characterizes multi-arm Gaussian minimax-regret rules for a fixed covariance matrix and gives covariance plug-in asymptotics.
Constructs convergent finite-game approximations for minimax treatment choice after discretizing nature's action space.

body.tldr: One realized assignment per cluster identifies assignment-cell welfare margins but not the cross-policy coupling that determines the finite-population covariance. The proposal treats that failure as the design object. A total calibrated Horvitz--Thompson estimator projects the compatible multi-marginal coupling polytope to the sharp covariance set \(\{\operatorname{diag}(A/r)-\Xi\}\), and the design minimizes the worst compatible pairwise comparison variance under exact-count or nominal-label Bernoulli allocation. An explicit incomparable-covariance construction separates this image problem from selecting one conservative quadratic variance bound, linear-program duals certify directional supports, finite KKT witnesses certify global allocation optimality, and a finite-population central limit theorem yields an empirical-best simple-regret guarantee. The exact all-selector robust minimax-regret receipt remains an open question with a concrete multi-marginal and least-favorable-prior handle.

project_justification.gap: Two-stage saturation papers either impose covariance structure or use conservative variance formulas. Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje optimize a single conservative quadratic upper bound for a fixed design and estimator, while sharp variance-bound papers do not choose a saturation randomization and Gaussian minimax-regret papers condition on one covariance matrix.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is a design optimized over the joint covariance set compatible with all assignment-cell margins of one unrestricted fixed schedule.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the sharp finite coupling polytope, proves by an explicit incomparable pair that no single conservative covariance envelope represents it, supplies LP support certificates, and proves a convex exact-hit allocation theorem with necessary-and-sufficient finite KKT optimality witnesses and an assignment-based regret guarantee.

body.related_work: AronowGreenLee2014 is the scalar two-potential-outcome sharp-variance benchmark; Proposition 2 requires the new support program to collapse to its Fréchet--Hoeffding solution on a slice-constant two-policy face. GaoGeQian2025, published in AISTATS 2025, supplies the multi-marginal optimal-transport language for exact coupling sets and informs the finite type-polytope construction, but it does not contain the saturation-specific covariance projection or choose a randomization. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 characterizes admissible conservative quadratic variance bounds and optimizes one such bound for a fixed design and linear estimator; Theorem 2 gives an explicit compatible covariance image that no single conservative covariance envelope can represent sharply in every direction, and Theorem 3 instead optimizes the allocation over that full image. LiDing2017 supplies the assignment-only vector central limit theorem carried into Theorem 4. JiangImaiMalani2023 studies randomization inference and power for two-stage direct and spillover contrasts with the design distribution fixed. BairdEtAl2018 uses standard-error formulas to study power-oriented saturation design under maintained outcome structure. Joo2025 characterizes Gaussian minimax-regret rules at a fixed covariance. GuggenbergerHuang2025 develops fictitious-play numerical approximations after discretizing nature's action space; these two papers inform the open exact robust receipt but do not couple allocation, compatible covariance, and selector optimization. EggerEtAl2022 supplies the worked saturation-policy consumer rather than a theorem comparator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance-set image is sharp conditional on the full assignment-cell marginal table \(f\). A current one-shot trial estimates those margins only asymptotically, and prospective use therefore requires fixed external planning margins or an uncertainty set around them. The theorem does not identify \(\Xi\), does not replace it by zero, and does not claim that \(G(\Sigma(sr,\lambda))=s^{-1/2}G(\Sigma(r,\lambda))\).
body.honest_scope: The sharp covariance set for the total calibrated Horvitz--Thompson estimator, its support linear programs, the non-representability by one conservative quadratic covariance envelope, the robust pairwise-variance design, its KKT certificate, and the empirical-best regret bound are theorem targets. All conclusions are conditional on fixed external planning information \(f\) and the proposal-specific common-tie local boundary. The exact robust Gaussian minimax-regret design and a terminating all-minimizer receipt are open. On a two-policy slice-constant face the construction reduces to the established sharp two-margin variance bound. For \(n_0=6\) and \(m=(1,2,4)\), the odd \(15\)-cell slices force \(\Xi_{kk}\ge1/900\) in the balanced binary instance, so the diagonal endpoint is excluded.
